hints.title: Operation Periodicity and Parity
hints.text: The four button actions repeat their pattern across every 6 lights, meaning only the first few light states determine the overall outcome.

hints.title: Small Values of Number of Bulbs and Button Presses
hints.text: Because pressing the same button twice cancels itself out, each button is pressed either 0 or 1 time net, leading to at most 8 possible states.

hints.title: Saturating Cases by Input Size
hints.text: When presses is zero return 1. If n is 1 return 2. If n is 2, return 3 when presses is 1, else 4. For n >= 3, return 4 for 1 press, 7 for 2 presses, and 8 for 3 or more presses.

complexity.notes: Optimal solution running in O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating full light array over all button permutations is redundant due to periodic modulo-6 behavior.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant time mathematical case distinction uses zero memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize operation symmetry and independence among initial bulb configurations.
